- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.5) over recent days, model tends to under-forecast upward momentum; adjust forecast upward by 1–2% of recent mean.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.2) or volatile, model often over-anticipates correction; reduce forecast by 1–3% to avoid overshoot.
- Model frequently overreacts to recent spikes (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days) by overshooting +5–10% in next forecast; cap upward revisions at +3% unless sentiment confirms continuation.
- Mean reversion bias: if 3–5 consecutive days show downward trend, model often fails to recognize reversal; add 0.5–1.5% upward bias if sentiment shifts to neutral/positive.
- For 30-day horizon, model underestimates late-period volatility (especially after sentiment spike); add 0.5–2% upward buffer if sentiment >0.6 in last 5 days.
- If sentiment is flat or mixed (0.2–0.5), model often misses structural shifts; use 1–2% smoothing filter to avoid overfitting to short-term noise.
